function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** (in finance/wealth‑management terms) refers to a formal instruction or authorization given by a client to a financial institution—such as a bank, investment firm, or wealth manager—to act on behalf of the client in managing assets, executing trades, or handling other financial activities. Key points: | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Purpose** | Enables professionals to manage investments, execute transactions, or perform fiduciary duties under agreed rules. | | **Types** | • *Active* – currently valid and enforceable.
• *Pending* – awaiting approval or activation.
• *Inactive* – expired, revoked, or otherwise not in force. | | **Scope** | Can cover specific accounts, asset classes, risk limits, or broader portfolio management responsibilities. | | **Legal Basis** | Often governed by regulatory frameworks (e.g., MiFID II in Europe), ensuring transparency, suitability, and compliance. | In practice, when you see “partner mandates” it means the mandates issued to your organization’s partners; “client mandates” refer to those held directly by individual customers.
